newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta Gas proposes regulatory changes.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta Gas proposes regulatory changes.

text.p: Atlanta Gas Light Co said it proposed a new regulatory framework Tuesday that would result in lower rates and greater customer choice for the company's residential and small business customers.

The plan, introduced at the second meeting of the Senate and House Competitive Natural Gas Service Study Committees, would closely follow the federal model used for the sale and transportation of natural gas to local natural gas distribution companies and large customers, the AGL Resources Inc subsidiary said.
The interim study committee was appointed to examine Georgia's natural gas industry and develop recommendations on measures for next year's legislative session.
The company noted competition already exists for the sale of natural gas to industrial customers.

"This plan responds to requests we heard from some of our larger customers during last year's legislative session," the utility said, adding it encourages competition for the supply of natural gas to all customers -- including residents and small businesses.

It said the proposal would create a reasonable transition period to ensure that there is sufficient competition among alternative services provided for small-volume customers. While Atlanta Gas Light would no longer sell natural gas, it would continue to provide delivery services through its statewide network of pipelines.
The proposal also provides for performance-based regulation of natural gas delivery, the company said.
If enacted next year, the Georgia Public Service Commission would be authorized to establish a series of incentives and disincentives that would compensate for providing quality service.
